# Global University AI Policy Audit 2026

> Open dataset: 186 audit records of whether universities publish official
> guidance on generative AI use. By Study Intelligence (https://aclas.si).
> License: CC-BY-4.0. Snapshot: 2026-10-14.

## What question does this answer?

Do universities publish official, public guidance on student/staff use of
generative AI? Each row was verified by opening a page on the university's
own official domain.

## Key findings

- 144 of 186 (77%) publish verifiable AI guidance; 24 confirmed none; 18 unclear.
- Top-50 universities: 92% publish guidance. Global South flagships: 46%.
- Zero campus-wide AI bans in the top 100. The global norm is delegated
  permission (instructors set per-course rules) plus mandatory disclosure.
- The policy gap maps onto the wealth gap.

## Files

- `ai-policy-audit-2026.csv` — 186 rows, 14 columns (UTF-8)
- `ai-policy-audit-2026.json` — same data plus dataset metadata
- `METHODOLOGY.md` — audit method, definitions, caveats
- `parse.py` — exact script that generated CSV/JSON
- `CITATION.cff` — machine-readable citation

## Columns (CSV)

`id`, `sample` (qs_top_50 / qs_51_100 / qs_101_150 / global_south), `rank`
(QS 2026), `university`, `country`, `has_policy` (YES / NO / UNCLEAR),
`policy_url`, `page_title`, `date_info`, `scope`, `note`, plus overlap flags.

## Caveats

- 15 universities appear in two samples (flagged `name_overlap`); deduplicate
  on `university` for institution-level counts (171 unique).
- UNCLEAR means "could not verify", not "confirmed absent".
- Snapshot 2026-10-14; policies change — verify before citing a single row.

## Citation

Study Intelligence (https://aclas.si). "Global University AI Policy Audit
2026" (v1.0.0, 2026-10-14). CC-BY-4.0.
